phrase.text: A subroutine is also a value: it can be stored in a variable, passed as an argument or returned, and called later.

runs.text: The type of a function describes its parameters and its return, for example
. Any subroutine with that shape is a value of that type. A function-typed variable is called as if it were the subroutine itself.

entries.text: Only variables that are never reassigned after getting their value can be captured: that way the copy and the original cannot diverge.
Functions are not written, not compared and do not cross between tasks.

runs.text: Capturing a variable that changes afterwards is an error, because the closure would see one value and the rest of the program another:

blocks.title: Capturing something that changes

diagnostics.message: Cannot capture n of type integer: it is reassigned or is a by-reference parameter

with the captured copies. The environment outlives the subroutine that created it as long as someone can call the closure, and the collector frees it once nobody can.

points.text: A subroutine is a value of type
It can be stored, passed, returned and called.
An anonymous function captures copies of the variables it uses.
Only variables that do not change are captured.
